evidence: Lee (1980), Eqs. (1)-(2) specify the local variance, but do not supply a two-input variation bound. Herbert et al. (2016), Background and Conclusion, concern implementation and running time, not sharp BV perturbation coefficients.

Sharp two-input variation sensitivity of three-point median smoothing on finite paths: Median map depends on middle order statistic, not the Euclidean norm of adjacent differences; its sharp norm cannot imply the exact local-standard-deviation coefficients.

Finite-window morphology: sharp two-input variation and a boundary-weight transition: Morphological min/max maps have different piecewise-linear Jacobians, so bounds for them do not dominate the square-root quadratic window statistic.

Sharp bounded-variation stability transition for projection onto a discrete total-variation ball: Projection onto a global variation ball is not a moving local standard-deviation operator and neither statement implies the other.
